articles.title: EDCOM 2 cites gaps in classroom allocations
articles.summary: The Second Congressional Commission on Education found gaps in the distribution of classroom allocations, with some municipalities with the largest shortages allegedly receiving fewer classrooms.

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am
EDCOM 2 said the issue was raised during the Oct. 16 Senate committee on finance hearing on the Department of Education (DepEd)’s proposed budget for 2027.
EDCOM 2

MANILA, Philippines — The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) found gaps in the distribution of classroom allocations, with some municipalities with the largest shortages allegedly receiving fewer classrooms.

EDCOM 2 reportedly discovered that in DepEd’s 2026 classroom allocation, only 45.2 percent of the 332 local governments with the largest estimated classroom shortages were among the top recipients of planned classroom allocations.

EDCOM 2 co-chairman Sen. Bam Aquino said DepEd and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) should accelerate classroom construction and ensure that allocations translate into completed facilities.

For this year, DepEd has initiated multiple channels to speed up classroom construction, targeting to complete 18,950 classrooms. It tapped the DPWH, partnered with provincial and city governments, civil society organizations and Public-Private Partnership Programs (PPPs).

EDCOM 2 executive director Karol Mark Yee praised DepEd for its “extraordinary efforts in mobilizing different routes for classroom construction. However, we also highlight the need for strategic and responsive allocations to ensure that these resources go where they are most needed.”

The commission reported that seven of the 10 municipalities with the highest funds for 2026 classroom construction received allocations exceeding their estimated classroom shortages based on 2023 data. Meanwhile, several municipalities with substantial deficits remained short of the classrooms needed to accommodate their learners.

“For instance, Maragondon, Cavite was allocated 272 classrooms against an estimated shortage of just 64. In contrast, Tanza, Cavite, received 448 classrooms against a shortage of a whopping 869, while Naic, Cavite was allocated 356 against a deficit of 631,” it explained.
EDCOM 2 also raised concerns over delays in classroom construction, particularly under DPWH-led implementation.

Out of the P21.45-billion allocation for 6,000 DPWH-led classrooms under the FY 2026 program, only P1.87 billion, covering 533 classrooms, allegedly reached the award or near-award stage during the hearing. Another P7 billion, covering approximately 2,000 classrooms, had been advertised for procurement.
DPWH Undersecretary Lara Esquibil pointed to failed biddings and higher construction costs amid rising fuel prices as factors affecting the implementation.
EDCOM 2 is reportedly creating a classroom tracker for transparency on where the funds are going.

For 2027, the National Expenditure Program (NEP) reportedly proposes P30.55 billion for classroom construction, with an additional request of P23.5 billion from DepEd for the construction of 2,385 new classrooms, 69 Last Mile School buildings, 500 Learning Continuity Spaces, as well as repair of 3,500 classrooms, among others. — Neil Jayson Servallos

articles.title: Prices of candles, basic goods stable ahead of Undas
articles.summary: The Department of Trade and Industry said prices of candles and other basic goods are stable ahead of the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Trade Secretary Cristina Roque told reporters on the sidelines of the SGV Tax Symposium yesterday that there is no movement in candle prices so far.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said prices of candles and other basic goods are stable ahead of the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.
Roque said the prices of other basic necessities and prime commodities (BNPCs) also remain stable.
Apart from candles, the other BNPCs are canned sardines, canned meat, coffee, processed milk, instant noodles, condiments, laundry soap, toilet soap, salt, batteries, bottled water and bread.
So far, Roque said the DTI has not received requests for price adjustments.
“For now, no price increase,” she said.
The DTI is planning to convene a meeting with manufacturers of basic goods this week as part of the agency’s monitoring of supply and prices.
Roque said she also plans to visit facilities of sardine and meat firms.
Earlier this month, Roque visited the facility of Nature’s Spring-maker Philippine Spring Water Resources Inc. to check the supply of bottled water in the midst of El Niño.
“For those that are part of the BNPC, we want to check the supply. And then we also want to check their inventory,” she said.
“But for now, there’s no need to panic. The prices of BNPCs within the list of the DTI are stable,” Roque said.

articles.title: Philippines retains Tier 1 status in human trafficking report
articles.summary: The Philippines has maintained its Tier 1 ranking for the 11th consecutive year in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report, highlighting sustained government efforts to…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

The development was announced at a briefing by Interior and Local Government Undersecretary for Peace and Order Nestor Sanares, who also leads the country’s Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC).

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has maintained its Tier 1 ranking for the 11th consecutive year in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, highlighting sustained government efforts to prevent human exploitation, prosecute traffickers and protect victims.

Sanares pointed out that the Tier 1 status, the highest rating given by the US State Department, indicates that the Philippines fully meets the minimum international standards for the elimination of human trafficking through inter-agency coordination.

“This milestone underscores the continuing commitment of the Philippine government, through the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) and its member agencies, to strengthen prevention, victim protection, prosecution and partnership,” Sanares said.

The DILG official noted that the 2026 TIP Report credited key institutional interventions, including the mandatory nationwide rollout of a specialized Victim Identification System, an enhanced National Referral Mechanism, expanded IACAT prosecutorial task forces and the launch of the IACAT ProtectPortal.

Sanares made the announcement as the Philippines leads preparatory SOMTC sessions with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and dialogue partners China, Japan and South Korea ahead of the 20th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime.

articles.title: Peak power demand seen rising amid El Niño
articles.summary: The country’s peak electricity demand could jump by 10.7 percent next year as the “super El Niño” threatens to further intensify summer heat, according to the Department of…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The country’s peak electricity demand could jump by 10.7 percent next year as the “super El Niño” threatens to further intensify summer heat, according to the Department of Energy.
Latest DOE data showed peak demand could reach 22,231 megawatts in 2027, up from the 20,088 MW recorded earlier this year.
Peak demand refers to the highest amount of electricity needed at a given time, when households and businesses use the most power.
The DOE monitors peak demand to ensure the country has enough electricity to meet consumer needs and prevent power outages.
Despite the projected increase, Energy Undersecretary Mario Marasigan said the country would have a sufficient power supply amid the El Niño threat.
“We don’t see shortages,” Marasigan told reporters on the sidelines of the Philippine International Nuclear Energy Forum yesterday.
On the supply side, he said hydropower facilities would be the most affected by El Niño, with output potentially dropping by as much as 60 percent.
The DOE is also assessing how the climate phenomenon could affect the efficiency of solar power plants and the performance of biomass facilities.

“If there is no agriculture, there is no produce and then definitely we have no waste,” Marasigan said, referring to biomass plants that use agricultural residues and animal waste to produce heat or electricity.
This year, the DOE expects more than 2,700 MW of power projects across the country to be completed.
Another 4,758 MW in committed projects are also expected to come online next year, further boosting power supply.
According to Marasigan, the DOE’s current priority is to resolve power supply constraints in the Visayas to ensure the region can stand on its own.
“If the Visayas can meet its own demand, it will no longer need to import power or at least reduce its imports from Luzon and Mindanao,” he said.
The National Grid Corp. of the Philippines placed the Visayas grid under red alert from 5 to 6 p.m. yesterday following the forced outages of several large coal-fired power plants.
A red alert is issued when the power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid’s regulating requirements.
Since January, the Visayas grid has recorded 45 red alerts, based on the latest industry data.
Department of Agriculture’s action plan

The Department of Agriculture has presented a consolidated P61.99-billion action plan to mitigate the anticipated effects of El Niño on the country’s food production and rural livelihoods, while acknowledging P371 million in proposed interventions that remain unfunded.

Undersecretary for Operations Roger Navarro reported the plan’s presentation to Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. following the National El Niño Task Force meeting presided over by President Marcos last week, according to a memorandum outlining the meeting’s highlights.
The proposed spending package includes P6.2 billion already released under the government’s UPLIFT Program.

The remaining funding requirements and unfunded interventions underscore the importance of matching preparedness plans with timely financing and implementation as the country braces for possible drought-related disruptions.

“We need to plan ahead and ensure farmers have the support they need to cope with a potentially severe El Niño, including access to drought-tolerant rice varieties and other appropriate inputs,” Laurel said.
Among the proposed interventions without funding are cloud seeding operations and measures to manage red-striped soft scale insect infestation affecting sugarcane production.
The P371-million shortfall highlights competing demands on resources as authorities seek to protect crops and sustain agricultural output.

All government agencies were directed to adopt energy- and water-conservation measures, while early procurement and possible budget realignment were encouraged, subject to applicable procurement, budgeting, accounting and auditing rules. — Josiah Antonio, Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: ‘Kickbacks for Co, Bernardo increased under Romualdez’
articles.summary: Kickbacks for fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co and former Department of Public Works and Highways undersecretary Roberto Bernardo from flood control projects rose from 20 percent to 25 percent…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

Former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Undersecretary Engr. Roberto Bernardo sheds tears as he exposes the alleged corruption involving DPWH officials during the Blue Ribbon Committee hearing on Friday, November 14, 2025.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — Kickbacks for fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co and former Department of Public Works and Highways undersecretary Roberto Bernardo from flood control projects rose from 20 percent to 25 percent when Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez was speaker of the House of Representatives, former DPWH district engineer Henry Alcantara revealed yesterday.

During the continuation of the hearing on Romualdez’s bail petition for his plunder case before the Sandiganbayan Third Division, Alcantara said Co determined the 20 percent kickback, which he referred to as “commitments,” during budget deliberations in 2022.
The percentage increased to 25 percent in 2023. Alcantara said he did not know why Co sought the increase.
Alcantara explained that he would contact either Co or Bernardo to request funding, with separate lists provided to each to avoid overlapping appropriations and double payment of the “commitments.”

The money came from “advance payments” made by around 12 private contractors who had allegedly been prearranged to win bidding processes conducted by the Bulacan 1st District Engineering Office, which Alcantara previously headed.
The “commitments” were based on a list of projects sent directly to Co and Bernardo for inclusion in budget deliberations at the bicameral conference committee.
Alcantara said this differed from the “regular wishlist” prepared by district engineers for endorsement to the DPWH central office and subsequent inclusion in the National Expenditure Program (NEP).

During the redirect examination by prosecutors from the Office of the Ombudsman, Alcantara confirmed that the increase in the percentage began in 2022, when the NEP for the following year was being prepared and Romualdez was already House speaker.
Alcantara also said he would ask for a two percent share from the “commitments,” a request he described as “naglalambing” or a friendly appeal.
He recalled meeting Co around September 2021, when the latter was not yet chairman of the House committee on appropriations.
Around the same time, the first batch of up to three deliveries of “commitments” was made in storage boxes to Co’s two units on the 56th floor of Horizon Homes in Bonifacio Global City.
Subsequent deliveries were sent to Co’s house in the upscale Valle Verde village, this time in suitcases containing P30 million to P40 million each.
Alcantara added that Co would pay congressmen who proposed infrastructure projects included in the NEP because their names did not appear as project proponents.
During cross-examination, defense lawyers led by Thea Daep sought to establish that Romualdez was not House speaker when the deliveries took place.
Alcantara also admitted that his judicial affidavit and testimonies at other legislative hearings on the flood control scandal did not mention Romualdez.

Asked by Moreno who was the “most intelligent guy” behind the kickback scheme, Alcantara said: “I do not know who started it. When I was an Engineer II and project engineer, this had already been a practice. I do not know who came up with it.”

articles.title: Marcos, Japan PM discuss bilateral ties, ASEAN Summit
articles.summary: President Marcos and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi discussed various areas of cooperation, including defense, security and preparations for the upcoming 49th Association of Southeast Asian…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

In a statement, the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) said the two leaders discussed the 4th Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders’ Meeting, which the Philippines and Japan are scheduled to co-chair in November.
PCO

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi discussed various areas of cooperation, including defense, security and preparations for the upcoming 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits – which will be held in Metro Manila from Nov. 15 to 17 – during a phone call yesterday.
A Japan-led initiative, AZEC is aimed at promoting clean energy, reducing carbon emissions and supporting sustainable economic growth while strengthening energy security across the region.

During the AZEC Plus One Online Summit last April 15, Japan announced its $10-billion Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience or POWERR Asia initiative to support energy security and resilience across the region.

“During the phone call today, the two leaders also discussed various areas of cooperation, such as on the Luzon Economic Corridor, defense and security and Japan’s long-standing support to peace consolidation efforts in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao. The President and the Prime Minister likewise exchanged views on artificial intelligence cooperation and regional developments,” the PCO said.
Marcos and Takaichi last held a bilateral meeting on May 28 during the former’s state visit to Japan, when the two countries elevated their relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Meanwhile, Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said preparations for the ASEAN Summit are “time on target.”
Recto, who chairs the ASEAN National Organizing Council, presided over a command conference on Monday.

“With 20 heads of state in attendance, this is a meeting with a million moving parts, from convoys to conferences, from agenda to attractions to be visited, from security to seat plans, so failure on our part is not an option,” he said.

articles.title: Palace on envoy row: Apology can’t be forced
articles.summary: An apology should be given sincerely by the offending party and not demanded by the aggrieved, Malacañang said yesterday amid calls for Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to apologize to Filipinos…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — An apology should be given sincerely by the offending party and not demanded by the aggrieved, Malacañang said yesterday amid calls for Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to apologize to Filipinos for his recent threatening remarks.
“Saying ‘sorry’ or ‘I’m sorry’ cannot be demanded, it must come from the heart,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said at a media briefing yesterday.
Philippine Coast Guard spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela issued the latest call.

President Marcos earlier expressed intention to summon Jing for a meeting, but Malacañang later said Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro had already met with Jing and that it was awaiting the report from the official.
“No details have been relayed to us so far. So let us wait for the report from Secretary Tess Lazaro,” Castro said.
Lazaro on Monday called Jing’s statement “provocative” and “unacceptable” and “does not contribute to creating understanding.”
Marcos had said he would like to have a word with the Chinese diplomat on what the latter really meant when he said Beijing could “easily win” a conflict with the Philippines.

“It sounds very much to me like a threat, and it is not a very diplomatic statement to be made. So we perhaps would like to understand what exactly it is that he means,” the President told reporters on the sidelines of the 125th founding anniversary of the PCG on Oct. 16.
“I think that deserves a discussion between the ambassador and myself,” Marcos said then, when pressed if he was going to summon Jing.
It’s business as usual for trade and investments despite the ongoing row with China, according to the Department of Trade and Industry.
“For now, none,” DTI Secretary Cristina Roque told reporters when asked about the impact on trade and investments of the intensifying tensions between the Philippines and China.
Roque said the DTI has no contingency plan to mitigate the potential impact of intensifying conflict on trade and investments.
Instead, she said the agency is on wait-and-see and is focused on its deliverables.
“It’s hard to speculate so it’s best for us to just move, keep on working on our deliverables,” she said.
For Rep. Edgar Erice, Marcos should personally handle the controversy over Jing’s provocative remarks instead of delegating the matter to the foreign affairs chief.

“Let the President handle this situation. We are dealing with China, one of the world’s most powerful countries. We cannot afford to aggravate tensions through unnecessary insults and diplomatic quarrels without a clear strategic objective,” Erice said.

“My appeal is simple: let President Marcos lead, let the DFA pursue diplomacy and let the DND protect our national security. We need wisdom and strategic direction, not a contest of who can make the strongest or most provocative statement,” he said.
Up to Marcos

Other members of the House of Representatives said it’s up to President Marcos to decide on what he thinks is best to address the latest diplomatic row with China. They stressed, however, that Filipinos don’t deserve to be bullied, especially by China’s top diplomat in the Philippines.
“A threat is a threat. That is an option of the President – to expel those what we call lesser diplomats,” Rep. Terry Ridon said.
Rep. Gerville Luistro and Joel Chua said the Philippines should take a firmer stand but without deviating from diplomacy.

“We should not be victims of a bully in our own land. But I wish to be clear, we are advocating a peaceful avenue of addressing the conflict with China,” Luistro said. “We deserve the respect of the foreign envoys.”

Chua said that while he is open to tougher response to Jing’s veiled threats, Marcos has to weigh the consequences of any action to the country’s relations with China. “It was very offensive for us to be threatened inside our own country.”
At the Senate, Sen. Risa Hontiveros became the latest among her colleagues to demand Jing’s expulsion through Senate Resolution 746 that she file yesterday.
She said Senate is aghast at Jing’s action and “wishes to express its disapproval of the undiplomatic conduct of a foreign envoy.”
Under the Vienna Convention, the Philippines has the right to expel a foreign diplomat “at any time and without having to explain its decision,” she said.
The Chinese embassy, meanwhile, posted on Facebook its demand for Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. to take back his remarks calling China “troublemaker” and “biggest threat.”

“You should ask SND Gibo Teodoro to take back his China ‘troublemaker biggest threat’ rhetoric and apologize for wrongfully detaining Chinese workers and persecuting innocent Chinese language teachers,” the embassy said, addressing Rep. Leila de Lima who earlier called on the administration to expel Jing. — Delon Porcalla, Neil Jayson Servallos, Pia Lee-Brago, Louella Desiderio

articles.title: ‘Disruptor’ Cielo Magno challenges traditional pols
articles.summary: She still lacks name recall, does not belong to a political dynasty and does not have billions to spend.

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — She still lacks name recall, does not belong to a political dynasty and does not have billions to spend.

But former finance undersecretary Cielo Magno is hoping that Filipinos are ready for a “disruptor” who need not rely on patronage politics, and who can offer solutions to seemingly intractable problems faced by the nation.

“I’m here not to become a part of traditional politics. I’m here to disrupt,” she told The STAR’s online show “Truth on the Line” on Monday. “I don’t have to win to do that, but I want to use the election platform.”

A professor of public finance and institutional and health economics at the University of the Philippines School of Economics in Diliman, Magno is aware of the challenges ahead for a relative unknown like her aspiring for a national post.
But she said she wanted to elevate the level of public discourse on raging issues, going into an election year.
She is pinning her hopes on youths, who have been inviting her to deliver speeches.
At a recent meething with Filipinos in Milan, Italy, Magno, responding to a question, said she would seek a Senate seat in 2028.
Healthcare reforms, education, industrial policy for job generation and improved food security are among her priorities.
Magno has long been known as an advocate of judicious budgeting and utilization of public funds.
Among other things, she is also pitching for free medicine and expanded zero-balance billing in all public hospitals as part of her “ambitious” bid for a Senate seat in the 2028 elections.
If elected, she said among her priorities would be strengthening the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) and focusing on taxation and budget.
“Include coverage of medicine so that it can be free. Zero-balance billing should be expanded in all public hospitals and improve access to primary health care or check-ups,” she said.

Implemented by the Department of Health, the zero-balance billing program ensures eligible patients and PhilHealth members admitted to participating government hospitals can receive covered health services with minimal or no remaining hospital bill, subject to rules.
Magno said this proposal would be possible by transferring the allocation and operations of the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program to PhilHealth.

“Let PhilHealth administer it. So that the zero-balance billing, not just in a few hospitals, but we can do it in all public hospitals,” she said while calling on Congress to give an adequate budget for the state insurer.
PhilHealth needs more than P200 billion to operationalize and give promised benefits as the government initially proposed P74.45 billion for next year, which can run out by March, she said.

Magno’s proposal echoes concerns raised earlier by the Health Professionals Alliance Against COVID-19 over PhilHealth’s chronic underfunding and lawmakers’ reliance on discretionary medical assistance, including MAIFIP, which critics say can be used for political patronage.
“Why do we need to make it difficult for people to go to politicians just to get the services that we have already paid the premium through our tax to PhilHealth?” she said.

In addition, Magno, whose research includes mining, urged the government to establish a clear industrial policy to ensure the Philippines benefits from investments under the US-led Pax Silica initiative.
She questioned whether the government had set conditions to ensure local industries would benefit from the investments.

“It will only become an opportunity for Filipino people if we have a clear vision, if we have a clear strategy to ensure that Pax Silica will be beneficial to us. But we don’t have a clear industrial policy framework that we can use to ensure that we will benefit from this,” she said.
“It’s like we just offered this land, a free lease and you come here. But how do we benefit from that? It’s not clear to me,” Magno added.

articles.title: Jonvic: No evidence linking Dutertes to Laos drugs
articles.summary: Authorities have no evidence linking the Duterte family to the 512-kilo shabu shipment seized in Laos, according to Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, even as he noted that alleged drug financier…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. holds a press conference at the PNP headquarters in Camp Crame, Quezon City on May 10, 2026.
The STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — Authorities have no evidence linking the Duterte family to the 512-kilo shabu shipment seized in Laos, according to Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, even as he noted that alleged drug financier Edrieza Rimbang has long been a political ally of the family.

“There is no evidence pointing to (involvement in the shabu shipment), but there is evidence that they know each other,” Remulla told reporters on the sidelines of the 20th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime.
Remulla said Rimbang and members of the Duterte family had been political allies for years, having run under the same party.

He stressed that such association alone does not establish involvement in the drug shipment. But he wondered why Rimbang, whom Remulla described as a known drug personality, was not placed on the narco watchlist during former president Rodrigo Duterte’s anti-drug campaign.
Remulla described Rimbang as a financier and the head of his own organization, but said he was only one of several people being investigated in connection with the drug trade.

He contrasted Rimbang’s case with that of former Iloilo City mayor and current Interior undersecretary Jed Patrick Mabilog, who he said was included in the drug list despite having no involvement in illegal drugs.
Remulla argued that the cases illustrated the consequences of an anti-drug campaign that failed to observe due process.

Mabilog left the country after claiming that his life was in danger following his inclusion on the drug watchlist. Remulla said the former mayor was among those who suffered from accusations that were not adequately tested in court.
The DILG chief said authorities were also investigating other people who may have been involved in the Laos shipment, adding that Rimbang was not necessarily the head of the entire network.
National security

After failing to pin impeachable offenses against her, the Vice President said the government shifted tactics by raising national security issues against her – an alleged Chinese-backed business venture and a drug bust in Laos.
In a statement issued yesterday, Duterte said the government is stretching the story to make it appear that there is a conspiracy.

“When the House of Representatives prosecution team failed to establish a convincing case of an impeachable offense, all it could offer were wacky poses that were neither entertaining nor amusing,” she said.

“Now, we are witnessing an apparent shift in the government’s narrative in taking me down, attempting to reframe the matter as a national security issue. Every thread seems to be stretched into a conspiracy – from a business venture allegedly linked to Chinese funding to a drug bust in Laos supposedly connected to a Mindanao-Davao conspiracy,” Duterte added. — Evelyn Macarian, Helen Flores

articles.title: OVP budget hearing done in 16 minutes
articles.summary: Despite a break in her impeachment trial, Vice President Sara Duterte snubbed her office’s budget hearing at the Senate yesterday and instead attended the inurnment of her longtime city planner…

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 12:00am

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian looks on as Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff of the Office of the Vice President, delivers her remarks during the Senate hearing on the OVP’s proposed 2027 budget on October 20, 2026.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Despite a break in her impeachment trial, Vice President Sara Duterte snubbed her office’s budget hearing at the Senate yesterday and instead attended the inurnment of her longtime city planner in Davao.
But the senators still approved for plenary debate the Office of the Vice President (OVP)’s proposed P785-million budget for 2027 after just 16 minutes of hearing by the Senate finance committee.
The OVP’s proposed 2027 budget is down 11 percent from its 2026 approved budget of P889 million.

OVP chief of staff Zuleika Lopez and assistant chief of staff Lemuel Ortonio represented the Vice President. They had also attended the previous impeachment trial, with Ortonio testifying as the prosecution’s hostile witness on the impeachment article on confidential funds misuse.
When Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian asked Lopez about Duterte, Lopez said Duterte is representing her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, in the inurnment rites.
Gatchalian said the Senate is hoping the Vice President would appear for the plenary debate of her agency’s budget.
“We hope she can give time to represent her office and defend your budget in plenary,” Gatchalian said.

When Senate finance chairman JV Ejercito asked if the OVP wanted the Senate to augment their budget for their ongoing free bus ride and livelihood programs, Lopez said the office would only “recalibrate” and not ask for more funding even though it would reduce their number of beneficiaries.
Duterte’s allies Sen. Imee Marcos and Sen. Bong Go moved for the committee approval of the OVP budget due to parliamentary courtesy.
Ejercito lauded the OVP for pushing through with their programs despite their limited budget, as he hoped for “unity” in the country despite the “political noise.”

articles.title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
articles.summary: Janine Lochrenberg, 65, was out on her daily morning swim with her club when she was attacked, her family tell the BBC.

blocks.text: A South African woman has been killed in a shark attack off the country's east coast, in what is the first recorded such fatality this year.
Janine Lochrenberg was swimming off a beach in KuGompo City (formerly East London) on Tuesday morning when she was attacked.
Witnesses said the 65-year-old was bitten in two places and died before she was brought to shore.
Shark attacks are rare in South Africa, with about 10 fatal ones since 2012, according to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File.

Lochrenberg was out on a daily morning swim with her local open water swimming club when she was attacked at around 08:00 (06:00 GMT). Fellow swimmers brought her to shore, but it's believed she died before they could get her out of the water.
She was bitten on her thigh and her upper arm, one of her fellow swimmers told the BBC. They also said she had been wearing a magnetic shark repellent band on her ankle at the time.
Lochrenberg's sister Margot said she was holding her sister's head as they brought her to shore but believed she bled out in the water.
She told the BBC that her sister had "loved the water so much" despite knowing there was an "elevated shark presence in East London".
"She'd made peace with that. She had a deep affinity with the water and was a remarkable person," she said.
Barbara Briceland, Lochrenberg's partner, told the BBC the retired medical physicist was a good swimmer, who often swam far out into the breakers, and described her as very brave.
"She was highly intelligent, lots of fun, kind, in a quietish way, thoughtful, well-loved with a love of life."
Briceland added they were looking forward to retirement and were about to leave for a three-week road trip together.
Orient Beach, where the attack took place, has been closed alongside another nearby beach, authorities confirmed.

articles.title: Alberta votes overwhelmingly to remain part of Canada
articles.summary: The vote has been hailed by Prime Minister Mark Carney as "a clear choice" in favour of national unity.

blocks.text: 'Conversation far from over': BBC reports from pro-separatist watch party
ByNadine YousifReporting from Edmonton and James FitzGerald
People in Alberta have voted overwhelmingly to stay in Canada, rejecting a proposal to pursue separation through a binding referendum.
With most votes counted, more than two-thirds of voters in the province had chosen to remain part of the country rather than pushing for independence, according to Elections Alberta, external.
Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday that "it's a great result for Canada" and he is "thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity".

The vote was called earlier this year by the province's leader, Danielle Smith, in response to a public petition. Smith herself opposed the separatist push but said the public will for a vote was undeniable.
She welcomed the initial results, commenting: "Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada."
Smith said she would address Albertans later on Tuesday on the path forward for the province.

In making the case for independence from Canada, many of the separatists said the oil-rich province's economic growth had been stifled by the environmental policies of Canada's central government in Ottawa.
But those who opposed a breakup - including Carney - called for Canada to present a united front in the face of external pressures, including an ongoing trade war with the United States.

Speaking to reporters as he walked into a Cabinet meeting in Ottawa on Tuesday, Carney said he had spoken to Smith that morning and discussed "moving forward in the spirit of cooperative federalism, including on issues of immigration, other common priorities".
But at a pro-separatist watch party in Edmonton, the hum of upbeat chatter quickly quieted as those present saw the projected results.
After overnight vote projections were published by Canadian broadcaster CBC and others, the mood soured. The watch party attended by the BBC packed up quickly, and people went home.
One of the separatist leaders, Jeffrey Rath, struck a defiant tone, however, vowing that "our movement isn't stopping and we're continuing to move forward".
Speaking to the BBC World Service's Newsday programme, Rath, a lawyer based in Calgary, said he saw Monday's vote as a "first step" which had taught the movement some "valuable lessons".

Asked whether his movement would push to keep holding votes on independence until it got the result it wanted, he responded "why not?", and insisted that "the math and the economics" all added up on his side of the argument.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Separatist leader Jeffrey Rath was defiant even as results went against him

blocks.text: Separatist leader Jeffrey Rath was defiant even as results went against him
Smith called the vote in response to a grassroots group gathering about 300,000 signatures on a petition that asked for a binding referendum on separation.
The petition was blocked by a judge, saying it failed to consult indigenous First Nations people - however, Smith opted to go ahead with the ballot.
Another group collected signatures for its own petition that opposed separation, which was signed by more than 400,000 people.

The key question on Monday's voting paper asked: "Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?"
Smith said before the vote that if voters chose the first option, a referendum on separation would not be held - at least, not while she was in power.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Those who favoured remaining part of the Canada cheered the result at an event in Edmonton

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Those who favoured remaining part of the Canada cheered the result at an event in Edmonton
Despite the projected results, the conversation around Albertan sovereignty is not over.
Separatists leaders have indicated that they plan to push Smith out of power within her United Conservative Party, in the hope of installing a leader who is more sympathetic to their cause.
Another separatist leader, Mitch Sylvestre, told the BBC on polling day that "a lot of work will have to be done" to curb the appetite for independence if his side did lose.

Canada has grappled with challenges to its unity before. The province of Quebec held two referendums on independence, in 1980 and 1995. Both were unsuccessful, but Alberta separatists believe Quebec used the threat of independence to gain significant political leverage over Canada's central government.
Although responses to the referendum question were tallied first, there were nine other non-binding questions on Monday's ballot paper.
Five of these dealt with immigration, while the other four focused on the Canadian constitution.
Early results suggest that most will pass, including proposals for the province to take increased control over immigration levels.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff
articles.summary:
Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody it

To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious…

blocks.text: To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.

But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.
Rather than drawing attention to the incumbent’s alleged misdeeds, many of the programme’s millions of viewers sarcastically took Bolsonaro’s hand-written message as an admission of his own guilt.
Following Sunday night’s debate, Lula supporters from all walks of life have flooded social media with photographs of their own self-descriptions inked on their palms.
John Ulhoa, the guitarist from a pop rock band called Pato Fu, jokingly described himself as a “musician (and a hunk)”.
Allow Instagram content?

This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.
The Emmy-winning comedian Antonio Tabet introduced himself to his 2.8 million followers on X as an artist.
Carlos Marcio used both palms to portray himself as a cellist and author.
Carla Emanuela Sacramento, an obstetric nurse, posted a photograph of herself clad in personal protective equipment and with the words “primary health care nurse” proudly written on her right palm.

Prominent politicians also jumped on the trend, including Lula’s health minister, the infectious disease specialist Alexandre Padilha, whose palm noted he was a doctor, and Tabata Amaral, who identified as a political scientist and astrophysicist.

All across the country, librarians, oil workers, engineers, journalists, architects, pilots, psychologists, seamstresses, street cleaners, teachers, influencers, and police officers used ballpoint pens to inscribe their professions on to their skin.
Writing on Substack, the Latin America expert James Bosworth called Bolsonaro’s stunt a “critical error” in his bid for power.

“It may have seemed like an inspired pre-debate gimmick. Instead, he gave the world a meme image that will stick with him for the rest of his political career,” Bosworth said, offering politicians a word of advice.
“Don’t write the word ‘corrupto’ on your hand and show it to the audience,” Bosworth suggested.

Bolsonaro, who is the son of the jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, is a professional politician who has long faced corruption accusations, although he denies them and has never been convicted. The 45-year-old senator also has well-documented ties to members of Rio’s mafia underworld and once employed the relatives of the city’s most notorious contract killer, Adriano da Nóbrega. Last week two allies were arrested for alleged involvement with the Red Command drug faction, which Donald Trump recently designated a foreign terrorist organisation. Bolsonaro voiced surprise at those arrests and said the men had the right to prove their innocence.
On Monday, Brazilian media reported that Bolsonaro was being investigated by the federal police as part of a money-laundering inquiry.
Lula, whose Worker’s party (PT) has also been involved in major corruption scandals, used Sunday’s debate to throw down the gauntlet to Bolsonaro.

The leftwing incumbent said he would give electoral authorities access to his banking and phone recordings, and those of close relatives, in order to prove he was not corrupt – if Bolsonaro agreed to do the same.

Bolsonaro, who, polls suggest, holds a slender advantage ahead of Sunday’s second-round runoff, has yet to respond to Lula’s challenge. The rightwinger won the 4 October first round by more than 2m votes.

articles.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
articles.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more…

image.caption: The released material reportedly included emails sent by party figures as well as bank statements, academic certificates and membership listsImage: Felix Kästle/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026last updated October 20, 2026
Far-right AfD says emails stolen in September cyberattack

Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was looking into the theft and subsequent online publication of emails stolen by unidentified hackers during a cyberattack last month.
An AfD spokesperson said the hackers had targeted a hosting provider used by the party and appeared to have copied data from a small number of mostly inactive email accounts.

"The recent online publication of what is presumably a portion of this data is currently being investigated," the spokesperson said. "A preliminary assessment can only be provided once this investigation has been concluded."
Although the spokesperson did not say how much data was stolen, an earlier report by the mass-circulation daily Bild put the number of AfD-linked emails published at more than 420,000.
According to Bild, the material published included not only emails sent by party figures such as co-leader Alice Weidel but also bank statements, academic certificates and membership lists.
The website hosting the material was offline by Tuesday afternoon.
However, archived versions showed a volume of 281 gigabytes of data under the headline "The party's own records, unedited."
The emails and other materials published have not yet been certified as authentic by any independent body.

The AfD, several state chapters of which have been classified as "confirmed right-wing extremist" by regional branches of Germany's domestic intelligence agency, has been topping recent national opinion polls and made gains in recent state elections.
Some politicians and civil society groups have called for it to be banned, arguing that the party is a threat to democracy, an accusation the party has rejected.

articles.title: Brazil's Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro tied ahead of runoff vote
articles.summary: With just under a week to go before the decisive presidential runoff election, polls show left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro are virtually…

image.caption: Both candidates faced off in a televised debate on SundayImage: Nelson Almeida/AFP

blocks.text: There are only a few days left until Brazil's runoff election on October 25, with neither left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva nor right-wing populist Flavio Bolsonaro a clear favorite.
While three polls from last week showed a razor-thin lead for Bolsonaro, the PoderData polling institute has now projected 50% voter backing for each candidate.
Brazil election: Lula faces Flavio Bolsonaro in runoff

This election could end up as close as the one held in 2022, when Lula narrowly beat Flavio Bolsonaro's father, Jair Messias Bolsonaro, with just 50.9% of the vote. Jair Bolsonaro, incidentally, was later jailed for attempting a coup to hold onto power.

His son, Flavio, surprisingly won the first round of voting on October 4 by securing 47% of the vote. Bolsonaro's right-wing bloc also won many additional seats in Congress, primarily at the expense of Brazil's centrist parties. And in the week following the first round of voting, polls showed Bolsonaro commanding a lead of up to six percentage points.

blocks.caption: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's large rallies have helped mobilize his supportersImage: Silvia Izquierdo/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Yet last week, Lula managed to gain momentum through nationwide mass rallies and his dynamic social media presence. Bolsonaro, in contrast, had scaled back street campaigning in light of his strong poll numbers.
That turned out to be a mistake. Now he, too, is once more mobilizing supporters to stage major rallies across Brazil as the country readies for the runoff.
A polarized nation
The rivalry between Lula's left-wing camp and Bolsonaro's far-right bloc has shaped Brazilian politics for the past decade.

Jair Bolsonaro gained nationwide recognition during the 2016 impeachment proceedings against Lula's political protegee, then-President Dilma Rousseff. He went on to win the 2018 presidential election while Lula was serving a prison sentence on corruption charges.
But when Lula's conviction was overturned, the former trade union leader staged a political comeback in 2022.

blocks.caption: Brazilian politics has become deeply polarizedImage: Cris Faga/Sipa USA/picture alliance

blocks.text: This polarization is responsible for the disappearance of centrist parties and a political alternative, or "third way," said political scientist Marco Aurelio Nogueira.

"The divide between Lula and Bolsonarism has paralyzed Brazilian politics, and anything that didn't belong to one pole or the other has disappeared," Nogueira told DW. This polarization is fueled by social media, the expert added, saying that "platforms' algorithms thrive on conflict and reward excitement."
Flavio Bolsonaro a toned-down version of his father
Nogueira said Flavio Bolsonaro's calm demeanor could explain why he has a realistic chance of defeating Lula, unlike his father in 2022.

"Jair Messias Bolsonaro was a crude, rhetorically aggressive figure," said Nogueira. "Flavio Bolsonaro, on the other hand, casts himself as more moderate and gives Bolsonarism a more youthful image. He communicates skillfully, posts well-produced videos, and addresses workers' issues, such as the introduction of the five-day workweek."

Lula's recent promise to shorten workweek hours has lent momentum to his campaign. Alarmed by Lula's rising poll numbers, Bolsonaro gave up his opposition to the move and voted in favor of the five-day workweek.

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro's backers also support his father, Jair BolsonaroImage: Alexandre Meneghini/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bolsonaro is now taking a less radical stance on fiscal policy, too. Although he had announced drastic budget cuts before the first round of voting, modeled on the policies of his libertarian Argentine ally Javier Milei, he now intends to continue Lula's social programs. That said, Bolsonaro has not presented a plan for how he intends to reduce Brazil's high public debt.
Banco Master corruption scandal shapes race

The election campaign has been overshadowed by a massive corruption scandal surrounding the insolvent financial institution Banco Master. Daniel Vorcaro, the bank's former owner, is under investigation for fraud, money laundering and corruption.

Vorcaro is accused of having bribed decision-makers in the world of politics, finance and the judiciary. Several Supreme Court justices are said to be involved in the scandal, which involved dubious sex parties and millions in reported payouts. Judges from both the Lula camp and some appointed by Jair Bolsonaro are said to be tied up in the scandal.

Flavio Bolsonaro is alleged to have accepted goods and services from Vorcaro, including a €10 million donation for a film about his father's life. Yet Lula has not been able to capitalize on his rival's alleged failings. After all, his very own son is implicated in another corruption scandal. Moreover, Bolsonaro has repeatedly drawn attention to Lula's 2017 conviction for corruption, even though it was later overturned by the Supreme Court.
Friday's debate key to reaching voters
Political scientist Nogueira believes the mudslinging between both candidates over who is more corrupt has left voters jaded.

"There are constant reports about scandals and mutual accusations from all sides," said Nogueira. "As a result, the effect is essentially canceled out in the election campaign. The average voter tunes out and no longer attaches much importance to these accusations when making a voting decision."

blocks.caption: The upcoming debate will have a major impact on the election, experts sayImage: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS

blocks.text: Both candidates held their first live television debate on Sunday. On Friday, two days before the runoff election, they will face off once more on Brazil's largest broadcaster, Globo. The debate will likely have a significant influence on the October 25 vote.
Experts believe the key for both candidates will be to not be rattled by provocations from the other side. Concrete policies, in turn, will only play a minor role in the debate.

articles.title: Who are the women powering India's youth-led 'Cockroach' protests?
articles.summary: Facing online harassment and police detentions, women are taking to the streets of Indian cities in large numbers for the youth-led "Cockroach" protests. Amid a large-scale crackdown, they refuse to…

image.caption: A protester attempts to stop a bus carrying detained protesters in New DelhiImage: Priyanshu Singh/REUTERS

blocks.text: On July 20, Navkiran Natt and her partner set out for the magistrate's office in New Delhi to get married. They arrived to find a tense situation, with police gathering to break up a youth-led march on Parliament. Office staff — and couple's wedding witnesses — running late due to barricades.
The protest movement known as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had announced the march to demand the resignation of India's then-Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
The protesters were met with heavy resistance from security forces, who had deployed batons, tear gas shells and pellet-firing shotguns, leading to injuries and mass detentions.
Less than three months later, on October 10, Natt left home early in the morning and spent the day crisscrossing the locked-down Indian capital looking for a protest she could join.

"The success of this protest is not how many people will reach Jantar Mantar," she told DW, referring to the protest site in central New Delhi. "It's that even after all this barricading and state violence, people are leaving their homes to join."
What are these protests about?

The CJP began as a satirical online movement after the chief justice of India, Surya Kant, referred to unemployed young people as "cockroaches" in an offhand remark. The name is an ironic riff on the name of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

After succeeding in seeing Pradhan step down in late July, the CJP is now demanding the resignation of the country's controversy-hit Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after more than 130 million names were removed from draft electoral rolls nationwide.
India: Protesters jailed amid election row
With CJP leadership in judicial custody or under threat of detention, one name has fast become synonymous with the demonstrations: student leader Neha Bora, who prefers to use the pronoun they/them.

Bora has run through the streets to dodge police officials, climbed barricades in the face of security personnel, shouted slogans from detention vans, and addressed press conferences alongside CJP spokespersons and others.

blocks.caption: Student activist Neha Bora has been detained by authorities on multiple occasions during this wave of protestsImage: Kabir Jhangiani/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: They are the president of the All India Students' Association (AISA), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation (CPI-ML).
"In extremely disappointing, fearful, tyrannical times, people try to gather hope from whatever source they can … If these people are fighting, then probably we can also fight," Bora told DW.
"It is a responsibility that you owe to people," they added.
Women out on the streets in large numbers

The Cockroach-led demonstrations also come at a time when women and members of the LGBTQ+ community are calling for greater autonomy for women in the aftermath of the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in New Delhi late last month, placing the issue of safety in India back into the spotlight.

According to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), 441,534 cases of crimes against women were registered in 2024, averaging 1,210 cases per day. Experts say these official statistics can only give a partial account of gendered violence.

blocks.caption: Women protesters have been taking to the streets in large numbersImage: Arun Sankar/AFP

blocks.text: But despite facing sexualized backlash from police on the streets and from online mobs, the women and genderqueer people leading the movement reject being cast as victims.
"The "beti bachao" [save the daughter] thing just doesn't cut it with this generation. It is a very specific ask: see us as political beings, free beings," activist Kavita Krishnan told DW.
"Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" (Save the Daughter, Educate the Daughter) is a flagship BJP government program launched in 2015.
Protest as daily life
These days, Gurmeher Kaur's day starts like any other — a workout or a yoga class — and often ends with Indian Youth Congress's lawyers getting her released from police detention.
"Resistance can't be a separate event … a big day, and then you go back to your regular life," she told DW.
The 29-year-old author of "The Young and the Restless: Youth and Politics in India" spent a better part of the last decade in the public eye.
This year, she joined the youth wing of India's main opposition party, The Congress, whose offices are located a stone's throw away from Jantar Mantar, the hub of the last wave of protests.
She said her political association has given her access to resources that can support the movement, offering a safety net for protesters "regardless of their political affiliation."
At a time when authorities are cracking down on CJP protesters, she said opposition members like her have a duty to fulfill: "Show up, put your body on the line."
The price of visibility
But showing up often comes with a cost, especially for women and queer protesters.
Kaur explains how male colleagues often "feel quite elated when their photos are in the media." However, for her, "attention is equal to death and rape threats and humiliation and abuse."
Natt, an activist most significantly associated with the 2020–2021 farmers' protests, echoes Kaur's experience.
"If a woman is leading the protest, the first attack is on her sexuality," she said.
Social media images have shown women protesters with their clothes torn during clashes with police.
Delhi officials have denied allegations of manhandling, adding that women protesters were treated with "dignity."
Bora refutes the police's claim, saying that a small number of female personnel were available to handle a large number of women protesters.
"Several women protesters came to protect me and prevent me from getting detained," they said.

Authorities have registered a police case against a journalist who accused a senior Delhi police officer of sexual harassment under an Indian law meant to prevent crimes against members of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). They say her own allegations are under investigation.
The internet was also flooded with AI-made, sexualized images of women protesters edited into protest photos.
Why activists say the tactic is failing
This has not prevented protesters from taking to the streets even the day after being detained by authorities.
"They don't know what they're dealing with," Krishnan said, referring to the government's crackdown on demonstrators.
She said authorities assume sexual humiliation will scare women off, but "this is not a generation that thinks of… sexual violence as being something shameful."

She was at the forefront of demonstrations after the 2012 "Nirbhaya" gang rape, where slogans like "Hang the rapists" were seen in public. This time, however, she said the anger "is not going to be about masculine displays of honor."
It is about "dignity and freedom ... Women face all kinds of problems in every country, and Indian women are no different," she added.

blocks.caption: Earlier this month, women took to the streets to demand stronger safety measures and greater accountability from the governmentImage: Sajjad Hussain/AFP

blocks.text: She said the youth-led protests are part of a wider global wave of "civilizational, cultural nationalism," which uses gender and the language of protection, whether of daughters, families or tradition, to rally support against minorities, immigrants and trans people.

"You listen to the rhetoric of Donald Trump or Viktor Orban or the Alternative for Germany (AfD). It is the same," she said, referring to politics in the United States and Europe. "If you look at what's happening in India, you may be able to better understand what's happening in your country."
These young Indians, she said, are refusing to be taken in. They are "fighting back for a language of the future, a language that has hope."

articles.title: Former Blue Jay, wife charged with fraud linked to Ontario youth baseball program fees: police
articles.summary: Former big leaguer Richard Butler and his wife, Michelle, have been charged after a fraud investigation into the Ontario Devil Rays baseball training program, which allegedly took thousands of…

image.caption: Michelle Butler, 52, and former professional baseball player Richard Butler, 53, are facing multiple charges after a fraud investigation focusing on the Ontario Devil Rays training program. (Durham Regional Police Services)

blocks.text: Toronto

Former big leaguer Richard Butler and his wife, Michelle, have been charged after a fraud investigation into the Ontario Devil Rays baseball training program, which allegedly took thousands of dollars for training it never provided, Durham police say.
Former big leaguer Richard Butler and his wife Michelle are facing 3 charges each

A former Major League Baseball player and his wife have been charged after a fraud investigation into an Ontario youth baseball program, which allegedly took thousands of dollars for training it never provided, Durham police say.

Between April 1 and Oct. 31 of last year, approximately $60,000 in registration fees for the 2025-2026 Ontario Devil Rays training program was deposited into a bank account associated with the program, police said in a news release Tuesday. But funds were later transferred to other accounts associated with the accused — Michelle Butler, 52, and former big leaguer Richard Butler, 53, both of Frankfurt, Ont.
The registration fees were allegedly not used for the program, and the services agreed upon were not provided, police said.

Families who paid the registration received an email on Oct. 19, 2025, saying the business had been dissolved due to financial hardship and claiming bankruptcy, police said. But investigators later determined the lawyer’s name on the email “had allegedly been used without his knowledge or permission, and no bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings were initiated,” the release said.
Rich Butler spent parts of three seasons in the big leagues, including a long sting with the Tampa Bay Devil Rays during the team's first season in the MLB. (Getty Images, David Seelig/Allsport)
Richard and Michelle Butler have now been charged with one count each of fraud over $5,000, possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000 and uttering a forged document.

Richard Butler played parts of three seasons in the big leagues, including seven games for the Toronto Blue Jays in 1997 and 79 games for the Tampa Bay Rays between 1998 and 1999, according to the Major League Baseball website.
Police say they are concerned there may be further victims. Anyone with information is asked to contact Durham police.

articles.title: Calgary police struggled with 'unprecedented' volume of information during search for Parker Wells: review
articles.summary: A review of the Calgary Police Service's response to the high-profile disappearance and search for an 11-year-old boy this summer found existing systems were not designed to manage the…

blocks.text: Calgary·New

A review of the Calgary Police Service's response to the high-profile disappearance and search for an 11-year-old boy this summer found existing systems were not designed to manage the "unprecedented" volume of information throughout the investigation.
Police to give update on internal review Tuesday at 9:30 a.m. MT

The internal review of the agency's "largest missing-person response" examined the successes and difficulties of the police investigation and found that, although public information efforts and interagency collaboration were strong, managing the scale of the investigation proved challenging.

One of the "greatest" challenges, the review found, was sorting through the approximately 1,000 formal tips and more than 90,000 social media messages received over the course of the investigation, in addition to thousands of emails and 10 terabytes of CCTV footage.

"The review found that while this information provided significant investigative value, existing systems were not designed to easily manage information at that scale during a prolonged critical incident," the review said.

Parker Wells disappeared from a specialized day facility on July 16, triggering an exhaustive search involving hundreds of police officers, alongside hundreds of trained searchers and volunteers. His body was found two weeks later in a system of underground pipes.
Investigators find body believed to be missing Calgary boy Parker | Hanomansing Tonight
Last month, a review of City of Calgary 911 procedures found the police dispatch was delayed by roughly one hour due to a lapse in adherence to procedure.
A review of the province's emergency alert system is currently underway.
The internal review noted it did not re-investigate the circumstances of Parker's disappearance, nor was it focused on assessing the performance of individual employees or partners.
"Like so many Calgarians, our members were deeply affected by Parker's disappearance and remained committed to finding him and supporting his family," Chief Katie McLellan said.

items: Calgarians gather at community vigil to remember boy found dead after lengthy search

blocks.text: "The review recognizes the efforts of our members, partners and the community throughout this response. It also challenges us to learn from the experience and identify ways we can strengthen future responses to major missing-person investigations and other prolonged critical incidents."
'Additional capacity' would have helped, review found
One of the investigation's successes, the review noted, was the widespread response of police and partner agencies in locating Parker.
It found more than 800 searcher deployments were contributed across CPS and its partners, commending the "commitment and adaptability" of the organization.

As the investigation grew more complex, however, the review found that "key personnel developed extensive knowledge that was difficult to transfer between shifts or personnel rotations and that many support functions were scaled up through individual initiative rather than formal surge plans."

"The review found that additional capacity and stronger organizational systems would have helped the CPS receive, assess, assign and track the extraordinary volume of information more efficiently," but that different resources or systems would not have changed the outcome.
As additional planning, logistics and resource co-ordination were added, roles and responsibilities were not always clearly understood, according to the review.

items: The emotional fallout for many Calgarians after search for Parker ends in tragedy

blocks.text: When it came to the volume of tips, the review found investigators often had to sort through duplicate information, while also verifying ownership and follow-up across separate systems.
Other findings looked at how, despite the crucial role technology played in the search, infrastructure and server capacity were also strained.

The review also made several recommendations for future missing persons cases, including establishing stronger clarity around staffing roles, developing a clearer alerting framework — especially for vulnerable missing persons — and creating a centralized tip-line to manage information volume.

items: Poilievre calls for reform to public alert system following disappearance, death of Calgary boy

blocks.text: In a statement included in the review, Parker's family said they appreciated the "thoroughness" of the review and "the commitment to learning from this tragedy."

"In a time of unimaginable fear and uncertainty, the response from everyone involved truly reflected the very best in people. We take great comfort in knowing that Parker’s life touched so many, and that his memory is helping shape meaningful changes," the family said.
Police are expected to speak about the investigation on Tuesday at 9:30 a.m. MT.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Kelsea Arnett is a reporter with CBC in Calgary. She began her career at CBC as a researcher during the 2023 Alberta provincial election and was a recipient of the 2025 CBC News Summer Scholarship. You can reach her at kelsea.arnett@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 200 people, sources say
articles.summary: A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.
articles.byline: Richard Kagoe, Lucy Fleming, Richard Irvine-Brown

blocks.text: Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 200 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral.

The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 73 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said.
A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF.

The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011.
South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. There are fears the conflict could spill across the border.
Despite a partial arms embargo on Sudan, foreign countries have been supplying both the army and the RSF with drones and they are increasingly becoming the weapon of choice in the conflict.
The war has created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, killed hundreds of thousands of people and forced more than 14 million from their homes.

"We are alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes across the country that are killing civilians, including children, and that are disrupting essential services," UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday, external.
The rising use of armed drones came as 20 million people faced acute hunger, with a rising risk of famine in parts of the western region of Darfur and Greater Kordofan, he said.
Greater Kordofan comprises three states and is a vital axis linking Darfur, controlled by the RSF, to the capital, Khartoum, now in army hands.

The attack in Abyei, which borders West Kordofan, took place on Monday around 11:30 local time (09:30 GMT) and had killed 73 people, the region's Information Minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Radio Tamazuj, which broadcasts from the Netherlands to audiences on the Sudan-South Sudan border.
"We were surprised by bombing and thick smoke inside Amiet Common Market, which is located 10km [six miles] from Abyei town," he said.

BBC Verify has studied satellite images that show extensive burnt buildings in the north-east corner of Amiet Market, which is also known in Arabic as Al-Na'am Market. Older images from the area show it is usually full of trucks.

It has also verified footage filmed near the market that shows a large plume of smoke, at least one petrol tanker and someone talking about five missiles being fired. Another verified video shows two massive, separate fires coming from buildings near that section of the market.
Ngor told the Reuters news agency that emergency workers had struggled to retrieve the bodies because of fires caused by the strikes.
Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said it had also received people wounded in the attack at Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town.

"So far we received over 20 patients, including several critical cases. Patients with burns were also admitted. We are providing surgical services and wound dressing, along with other emergency care," MSF's Christian Lindauer, the charity's manager at the hospital, said in a statement.
Meanwhile, a drone strike near the airport in Khartoum on Monday has killed four people, including three children, the AFP news agency reports, quoting a medical source.
It also cited a military source as saying air defences in the Sudanese capital had downed several other drones launched by the RSF towards the airport.
Fighting in Kordofan, a strategic area rich in gold and oil, has intensified over the last year after the army regained control of Khartoum from the RSF.

articles.title: Chinese warship, research vessel spotted at Bajo de Masinloc
articles.summary: A Chinese warship and research vessel were spotted in separate occasions by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in the waters of the Bajo de Masinloc.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 9:42pm
A Chinese warship and research vessel were spotted in separate occasions by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in the waters of the Bajo de Masinloc.
In a 24 Oras report from Chino Gaston on Tuesday, the PCG received reports that China was building structures in the Bajo de Masinloc.
GMA News joined the Coast Guard in a maritime domain awareness flight to the disputed reef that spotted a Chinese warship.
The Chinese ship even posed a radio challenge at the patrolling Philippine Air Force plane.
Right outside Bajo de Masinloc, there was a Chinese research vessel that was unaccompanied by the Chinese Coast Guard.

Within the lagoon of Bajo de Masinloc, there was one yellow buoy. A larger buoy that appeared to have an antenna was also spotted outside of the atoll; this was the same buoy that the PCG spotted one year ago.
Based on Gaston’s report, the PCG flight was not interfered with, which would have been typical behavior from the Chinese Coast Guard or the People's Liberation Army Navy.
Both of whom have been known to intercept Philippine aircrafts in Bajo de Masinloc.
The plane flew down to 200 feet but the reported infrastructure was not seen.
Newly-installed PCG Commandant Admiral Rommel Supangan said that the agency will continue to protect Philippine waters, based on the orders of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.

“Patuloy ang parte ng modernization ng Coast Guard. Kasama diyan ang ating pag-uusap sa Japan para sa karagdagang barko, ang 97 meters, gayundin sa France for the 35 meters na fastcraft,” Supangan said.
(The Coast Guard’s part in modernization continues. That includes talks with Japans for additional 97 meter boats, as well as with France for 35 meter fastcraft.) —Jean Mangaluz/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Huge setback for Alberta's separatist movement after decisive defeat
articles.summary: Leaders of the movement for independence vow to push on but the margin of defeat could make that difficult.

blocks.text: The outcome was celebrated almost immediately by Prime Minister Mark Carney, who said in a statement that "Albertans made a clear choice".
But the movement's leaders say their battle is long from over and that the issue could dominate Alberta politics for years to come.
Jeffrey Rath, a Calgary-lawyer and one of the main spokespeople for Alberta separation, said he and others "plan to roll up our sleeves and work harder".

Keith Wilson, another separatist, told supporters in Calgary that while the vote is over, "the conversation about Alberta's future in Canada and our place in Canada and our role in Canada will continue".
Smith, who openly supported and campaigned for the unity vote, thanked voters for the result.
The Alberta premier has been criticised for taking a "dangerous" gamble that the independence push would likely face defeat while still giving her restive base what they wanted.
She lowered the petition threshold needed to get the citizen-led campaign the ballot in the first place.

By making Monday's result non-binding, she got around a court decision blocking the pro-separation petition because it failed to consult indigenous First Nations whose land would be affected if the province separated.
That gamble could test her leadership of the United Conservative Party, which she has led since 2022.
"She's lost the confidence of the (party) base," said Rath.

Albertans who voted against an independence referendum told the BBC throughout the campaign that they were motivated by a desire to keep the country united, especially as Canada grapples with tariff threats from the US, its longtime ally.
They also feared that an independent Alberta could be vulnerable to outside influence - or even annexation.
Thomas Lukaszuk, a prominent pro-unity campaigner, told a crowd of supporters on Monday night that the early results made him proud to be Albertan.

At a pro-unity results watch party in Edmonton, Lukaszuk appealled directly to separatists, saying that "some of the issues they have raised are legitimate", and that the province must do the hard work of healing the divisions laid bare by this debate.
"I don't want to see us doing another referendum like this ever again," Lukaszuk said.
Premier Smith told CBC earlier in the week that she would not hold an independence referendum if Albertans vote against it as long as she is premier.
Some of the rifts can't easily be smoothed over.

The separatist sentiment has its roots in "western alienation" which is a term that has been used for decades by some in Canada's western provinces to describe a feeling of being ignored or overlooked by the federal government in central Canada.
She also put nine other questions to Albertans on Monday, most that seek to give the province more autonomy from Ottawa, including on matters like immigration.
The (very) preliminary results suggest that many might pass.

Some who voted in favour of a second binding separation referendum have said they didn't want outright independence, but some leverage over Ottawa. Smith has said these other nine questions help give her just that.
Quebec, another province with similar sovereigntist sentiments, could offer clues on where Alberta's separation movement might end up.
They held two separation referendums, in 1980 and 1995, both of which were defeated by a close margin.
Alberta independence supporters don't hide the fact that they gain inspiration from the majority French-speaking province.
They view Quebec as having successfully used the threat of separation to gain significantly more autonomy over provincial affairs.
And despite support for Quebec sovereignty being at historic lows, a newly elected provincial government has pledged to hold a third referendum on independence by 2030.
Rath made a note of that as he pondered his side's defeat.
The sovereigntist Parti Quebecois "has just formed the government of Quebec with 28% of the vote," he said.
"It's not out of the realm of possibility", he added, that Alberta separatists could do the same in the future.
